question.explanation: The range of $y = \sqrt[7] x$ is $ -\infty < y < \infty. $ Transformations do not change this interval. example.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Odd Index

question.explanation:
The range of $y = \sqrt[3] x$ is $ y \in (-\infty,\infty). $

Transformations do not change this interval. Therefore, the range of $f(x)$ is $y \in (-\infty,\infty).$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index

question.explanation:
The range of $\sqrt[6] x$ is

\[ \sqrt[6] x \ge 0. \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

\[ \sqrt[6]{2-3x} \ge 0. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $-3,$ we get

\begin{align*} \sqrt[6]{2-3x} &\ge 0 \\[3pt] -3\sqrt[6]{2-3x} &\le 0. \end{align*}

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x) \in (-\infty,0].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

example.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index

question.explanation:
The range of $\sqrt[4] x$ is

\[ \sqrt[4] x \ge 0. \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

\[ \sqrt[4]{5x + 2} \ge 0. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $-4,$ we get

\begin{align*} \sqrt[4]{5x + 2}&\ge 0 \\[5pt] -4\sqrt[4]{5x + 2} &\le 0. \end{align*}

Therefore, the range of the given function is $h(x) \in \left( \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{{-\infty}}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0} \right].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=h(x)$ is shown below.
